headline.label: live ISO boot to shell (Alpine: 3.1 s)

summary.conditions: `docker image inspect` and `docker save | gzip`, amd64. Alpine's image includes OpenSSL and a CA bundle; the KwickOS base has neither

summary.what: live ISO boot to shell prompt
summary.conditions: median (range) of 10 runs, wall time from QEMU start; QEMU/KVM q35, 2 vCPU, 512 MiB; each ISO with its own kernel (KwickOS `generic`, Alpine `virt`). KwickOS: the amd64 headless ISO built from main after 0.7.0 (see the raw file)

summary.what: guest boot time at the shell prompt
microVM boot (`virt` kernel, whole OS in RAM)
summary.conditions: QEMU `microvm`, release `kwickos-amd64.efi` and initramfs, median of 10 (guest 0.19-0.69 s, wall 0.40-1.15 s)

summary.what: memory in use after boot (live ISO)
summary.conditions: `MemTotal - MemAvailable` at the prompt, range of 10 runs (medians 66.3 and 49.6). Alpine keeps its root file system in RAM: 11 MiB of its 15 MiB shmem (the other 4 MiB is the QEMU display's framebuffer, which KwickOS has too). Without the RAM root Alpine is about 55 MiB, so KwickOS still uses about 5 MiB less like for like. The live root's LZMA dictionary is 64 KiB: with main's earlier automatic dictionary the kernel held 4 MiB of decompression buffers per CPU and KwickOS measured 53-59 MiB here (2026-11-23-vm-3-before.txt)
unique package names in Alpine main + community and in Debian trixie, trixie-updates and trixie-security main, the sources KwickOS's apt uses

`du -smx /` after installing, package indexes and caches removed. KwickOS 0.7.0 with kpkg, the documentation excludes and the lean rebuild of Debian's curl from main, not yet in a release (no LDAP, RTMP, GSSAPI or libssh2; Alpine's curl has none of these either). Most of the rest is glibc (13 MB, 8 MB of it iconv modules), perl-base for debconf (13 MB, needed by ca-certificates) and OpenSSL (8.7 MB, already part of Alpine's base image). Per-lever numbers: 2026-11-23-footprint-levers.txt

same. Both install the standard library's compiled bytecode (Alpine pulls in python3-pyc, 12.8 MB; Debian's postinst compiles 12.6 MB). KwickOS adds glibc, perl-base for debconf (tzdata), OpenSSL, tzdata and Berkeley DB

summary.what: installed size with nginx / openssh-server / git
summary.conditions: same. Debian's packages bring glibc, perl-base for debconf, OpenSSL, PAM and coreutils (openssh-server) and Perl with its modules (git, 52 MB); Alpine splits git-perl out

summary.what: live ISO download, amd64 / arm64 / riscv64
summary.conditions: release file sizes. Alpine `virt` ISOs; riscv64 has only the `standard` ISO. KwickOS ISOs carry the `generic` kernel and its modules

summary.what: memory of a `sh` in a container
summary.conditions: anon + page tables from the container's `memory.stat`, 5 runs. A real but trivial difference
